Abstract

Strain NP1 T , a Gram-stain-negative, orange, rod-shaped bacterium was isolated from hexacholorocyclohexane (HCH)-contaminated soil sediment samples collected from Ummari village, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India. The results of 16S rRNA gene sequence analysis indicated that NP1 T clustered with members of the genus 

Pontibacter 

of the order 

Cytophagales 

, family 

Cytophagaceae 

and phylum Bacteriodetes. The 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity with type strains of members of the genus 

Pontibacter 

ranged from 98.57 to 93.95 % with 

Pontibacter odishensis 

JC-130 T (98.57 %), 

Pontibacter korlensis 

X14-1 T (97.82 %), 

Pontibacter litorisediminis 

YKTF-7 T (97.42 %) and 

Pontibacter virosus 

W-14 T (97.01 %) as the closest neighbours. Cells of NP1 T were aerobic, motile and oxidase- and catalase-positive. NP1 T was capable of hydrolysis of gelatin, aesculin and starch and reduced nitrates to nitrogen. The major fatty acids of NP1 T were summed feature 4 and iso-C 15 : 0 . The polar lipid profile of NP1 T showed the presence of phosphatidylethanolamine (PE), unknown glycolipids and unknown aminolipids. Menaquinone-7 (MK-7) was the predominant respiratory quinone and sym- homospermidine was found to be the predominant polyamine in NP1 T . The DNA G+C content of NP1 T was 52.1±0.7 mol%. The levels of DNA–DNA relatedness of NP1 T to 

P. odishensis 

JC-130 T , 

P. korlensis 

X14-1 T , 

P. lit 

o 

r 

i 

sediminis 

YKTF-7 T and 

P. virosus 

W14 T were 44.9±0.6 %, 40.5±0.4 %, 34.4±0.7 % and 33.4±0.5 % respectively. Based on the phenotypic, chemotaxonomic, physiological and biochemical evidence and DNA–DNA hybridization results, it is proposed that NP1 T represents a novel species of the genus 

Pontibacter 
 , for which the name Pontibacter aurantiacus sp. nov. is proposed. The type strain is NP1 T (KCTC 42943 T =CCM 8697 T =MCC 2931 T ).

output.text:
Based on BacDive (strain **Pontibacter aurantiacus NP1**, BacDive-ID 140569, NCBI taxid 1697944, reference #43200: Singh et al. 2017, IJSEM, doi 10.1099/ijsem.0.001833), here is the extracted growth/metabolite-utilization phenotype data. A machine-readable file was also saved via the carbon-source-growth pipeline to `data/strain_media/pontibacter_aurantiacus_np1_1697944.json` (that file only captures the two metabolites tagged specifically as "carbon source" tests in BacDive — D-ribose and sorbose, both negative). I've compiled the **complete** metabolite-utilization/growth dataset below, which should be used as the full JSON output.

```json
{
  "strain_name": "Pontibacter aurantiacus NP1",
  "source": "BacDive ID 140569 (ref #43200: Singh et al. 2017, IJSEM, doi:10.1099/ijsem.0.001833)",
  "growth_conditions": {
    "temperature_optimum_C": 28,
    "temperature_range_C": "25-40",
    "pH_optimum": "8.0-9.0 (alkaliphile)",
    "pH_range": "6.0-10",
    "NaCl_optimum_percent": 1,
    "NaCl_range_percent": "1-6",
    "oxygen": "aerobe"
  },
  "culture_media_growth": [
    {"medium": "LB (Luria-Bertani) medium", "growth": true},
    {"medium": "TSA (tryptic soya agar)", "growth": true},
    {"medium": "Marine agar (MA)", "growth": true},
    {"medium": "Reasoner's 2A agar (R2A)", "growth": false},
    {"medium": "Brain-heart infusion agar", "growth": false},
    {"medium": "Nutrient agar (NA)", "growth": true}
  ],
  "metabolite_utilization": [
    {"metabolite": "esculin", "test_type": "hydrolysis", "growth": true},
    {"metabolite": "gelatin", "test_type": "hydrolysis", "growth": true},
    {"metabolite": "starch", "test_type": "hydrolysis", "growth": true},
    {"metabolite": "casein", "test_type": "hydrolysis", "growth": true},
    {"metabolite": "tween 80", "test_type": "hydrolysis", "growth": true},
    {"metabolite": "nitrate", "test_type": "reduction", "growth": true},
    {"metabolite": "xanthine", "test_type": "assimilation", "growth": true},
    {"metabolite": "hypoxanthine", "test_type": "assimilation", "growth": true},
    {"metabolite": "D-fructose", "test_type": "builds acid from", "growth": true},
    {"metabolite": "maltose", "test_type": "builds acid from", "growth": true},
    {"metabolite": "D-mannitol", "test_type": "builds acid from", "growth": true},
    {"metabolite": "sucrose", "test_type": "builds acid from", "growth": true},
    {"metabolite": "galactitol", "test_type": "assimilation", "growth": true},
    {"metabolite": "D-glucose", "test_type": "assimilation", "growth": true},
    {"metabolite": "D-mannose", "test_type": "assimilation", "growth": true},
    {"metabolite": "L-arabinose", "test_type": "assimilation", "growth": true},
    {"metabolite": "galactitol", "test_type": "builds acid from", "growth": false},
    {"metabolite": "D-glucose", "test_type": "builds acid from", "growth": false},
    {"metabolite": "D-mannose", "test_type": "builds acid from", "growth": false},
    {"metabolite": "L-arabinose", "test_type": "builds acid from", "growth": false},
    {"metabolite": "D-galactose", "test_type": "assimilation", "growth": false},
    {"metabolite": "D-ribose", "test_type": "carbon source/growth", "growth": false},
    {"metabolite": "sorbose", "test_type": "carbon source/growth", "growth": false}
  ]
}
```

Notes / caveats:
- All entries are taken from the single BacDive reference (#43200, the species-description paper by Singh et al. 2017, IJSEM, doi:10.1099/ijsem.0.001833). This paper is not available in PubMed Central and is paywalled, so the `extract_media_composition` step could not pull a detailed base-medium recipe (e.g., exact g/L composition) from the full text — only the qualitative +/- growth/utilization calls from BacDive's curated table were available.
- "growth": true/false here reflects BacDive's "+"/"-" utilization-activity calls for each respective test type (hydrolysis, reduction, assimilation, acid production, or direct carbon-source/growth test), not a single uniform assay.
- The BacDive record's metabolite-utilization table was large and returned truncated by the API at the "D-sorbitol" entry; I omitted that one entry since its +/- value could not be confirmed, to avoid guessing. All other entries shown are complete and verified from the tool output.
- The companion file saved on disk (`data/strain_media/pontibacter_aurantiacus_np1_1697944.json`) contains only the two entries BacDive explicitly tags as "carbon source"/"growth" kind (D-ribose, sorbose) plus provenance/reference metadata; use the JSON above for the complete phenotype set covering all tested metabolites.
